title: Two-stage leaderboard: proper-score qualification, then prospective escrow
ranking_rule: stage 1 (proper score, benchmark-relative, week-cluster lower bound, Holm-adjusted) qualifies; stage 2 (prospective CLV) is the escrow and is blank until a price source exists. No raw win rate is used.

rows.title: Moneyline: fair price when the rating edge is positive
rows.definition: p(home) = Phi(fair margin / SD); a game is bet only when p != 0.5. Scored with Brier.

staking.blank_reason: stage 2 needs a closing market price; no official price source exists (F-01), so CLV and ROI are not computed. Assumed -110 is deliberately NOT used any more: an assumed price cannot produce decision-grade ROI.

rows.title: Moneyline: only games with a fair margin of 6 points or more
rows.definition: Same forecast as S1, but the strategy passes on games below the 6-point edge. The Brier score below is computed on ALL games, so it is the forecast's skill, not the selection's - selection skill cannot be separated from variance at this n.

staking.blank_reason: stage 2 needs a closing market price; no official price source exists (F-01), so CLV and ROI are not computed. Assumed -110 is deliberately NOT used any more: an assumed price cannot produce decision-grade ROI.

rows.title: Control: a constant 0.5 forecast
rows.definition: Random picks expressed as a probability. Removes luck by construction: whatever score this posts is the score variance alone can produce.

staking.blank_reason: stage 2 needs a closing market price; no official price source exists (F-01), so CLV and ROI are not computed. Assumed -110 is deliberately NOT used any more: an assumed price cannot produce decision-grade ROI.

rows.title: Control: pick the home team, stated at 0.5+eps confidence
rows.definition: The favourite-free baseline. If a strategy cannot beat this on a proper score, it has no signal worth staking.

staking.blank_reason: stage 2 needs a closing market price; no official price source exists (F-01), so CLV and ROI are not computed. Assumed -110 is deliberately NOT used any more: an assumed price cannot produce decision-grade ROI.

rows.title: Control: the training-window home win rate in every game
rows.definition: The benchmark itself, scored as if it were a strategy. Its BSS must be exactly 0 because the benchmark term in every BSS is this same forecast; the script asserts it, so a nonzero value would mean the scoring arithmetic is broken.

removal_of_luck.title: Removal of luck

what_it_removes.how: no assumed price is used anywhere; stage 2 is blank
never reported as a metric; proper score instead
rules frozen in prereg before scoring
requires point-in-time availability for past games; the repository holds one week of it, so the ablation cannot be run and is NOT claimed

control_floor.reading: luck alone reached this upper bound on this n. A point estimate below the floor is indistinguishable from variance, whatever its p-value.

headline.why_the_adjustment_matters: unadjusted p = 0.0333 would read as significant at 5%; Holm across 5 strategies gives 0.1465, which does not clear. This is the multiplicity the brief requires, stated with the number of trials beside it.

removal_of_luck.verdict_computed: no strategy qualifies: the point estimate is positive and clears the control floor but the Holm-adjusted p does not clear 0.05
removal_of_luck.what_would_change_the_verdict: more independent weeks. The cluster bound scales roughly with sqrt(n_weeks); at the current spread it needs a substantially longer prospective sample, which is why stage 2 exists and why the escrow is empty today.
